grammar.title: Participle clause untuk tulisan yang ringkas
grammar.explanation: Participle clause memadatkan dua kalimat menjadi satu. 'Having + V3' berarti 'setelah', V-ing berarti 'sambil/karena', dan V3 bermakna pasif. Subjek kedua klausa harus sama.
examples: Having interviewed ten users, we noticed a clear pattern.
Designed for beginners, the app avoids technical terms.
Looking at the data, we decided to simplify the form.

common_mistake.wrong: Having interview the users, we changed the layout.
common_mistake.right: Having interviewed the users, we changed the layout.

grammar.title: Wish dan if only
grammar.explanation: Untuk harapan tentang keadaan sekarang, pakai wish + past simple. Untuk penyesalan tentang masa lalu, pakai wish + past perfect (had + V3). 'If only' artinya sama, tapi lebih kuat.
examples: I wish the app loaded faster.
I wish we had tested it on older phones.
If only we had more time before the launch.

common_mistake.wrong: I wish we tested it before the launch last month.
common_mistake.right: I wish we had tested it before the launch last month.

reading.title: Why fewer choices can make users happier
reading.text: In a famous study at a California supermarket, researchers set up a tasting table with either six or twenty-four kinds of jam. The larger display attracted more visitors, yet shoppers who saw only six options were about ten times more likely to buy a jar. Psychologists describe this as choice overload: when we face too many alternatives, the effort of comparing them increases cognitive load, and we often postpone the decision altogether. Later studies have shown that the effect is not universal; experts who know exactly what they want are less affected. Nevertheless, the lesson for designers is powerful. Navigation menus, pricing pages and settings screens frequently present every possible option at once. Having identified the few choices that most people actually need, designers can show those first and hide advanced options behind a single, clearly labelled link.

questions.q: What often happens when we face too many options?
What does the writer recommend to designers?
options: Show the most needed choices first

writing.prompt: Tulis kritik desain (design critique) untuk sebuah aplikasi yang sering kamu pakai. Jelaskan apa yang sudah baik, dua masalah utama beserta dampaknya bagi pengguna, dan usulan perbaikan yang bisa diuji. Gunakan nada profesional.
checklist: Dibuka dengan konteks aplikasi dan penggunanya
Dua masalah dengan dampak nyata bagi pengguna
Minimal satu participle clause (Having ..., Designed for ...)
useful_phrases: I would suggest two changes that could be tested ...
writing.model_answer:
Design critique: a popular food delivery app

Designed for people who are hungry and in a hurry, the app does a good job of getting users from the home screen to a finished order. The layout is visually consistent, restaurant photos are large and appetising, and the order tracking map is genuinely delightful. These details make the experience feel fast and trustworthy.

However, two problems stand out. First, the checkout page tries to do too much at once. Promotions, tip options, cutlery preferences and three payment methods all appear on a single screen. Having watched several friends use it, I noticed that most of them scrolled up and down repeatedly before paying, which suggests that the cognitive load is too high. Some users may even abandon their order at this stage.

Second, the delivery fee is only shown at the very end. At first glance the prices look cheap, but the final total often comes as a surprise, and this can come across as dishonest. Users who feel tricked are less likely to return.

To improve the experience, I would suggest two changes that could be tested with a small group of users. The checkout could be split into two short steps, with tips and cutlery moved behind an optional link. In addition, the estimated delivery fee could be displayed on each restaurant card. If both changes reduced drop-off by even a few percent, the impact on revenue would be significant.

speaking.focus: Bedakan 'we'd' dan 'we had', tekanan pada COG-ni-tive dan in-TU-i-tive, serta linking 'comes across as'.

speaking.prompt: Ceritakan sebuah proyek (kerja atau pribadi) yang tidak berjalan sesuai rencana. Apa yang terjadi, apa yang kamu sesali (pakai I wish ...), dan apa yang kamu pelajari? (5 sampai 6 kalimat)
speaking.sample_answer: Last year I built a budgeting app for my friends, but almost nobody used it after the first week. Having spent two months on it, I was pretty disappointed. Looking back, I wish I had shown them a simple prototype before writing so much code. It turned out they didn't want to track every expense; they just wanted a reminder before payday. The biggest lesson was that I should test the idea before I perfect the product. Now I always talk to at least five users before I start building anything.

n1.them: Hi, I'm Laura. I've never done a user interview before. What do I need to do?
hints: tenangkan: There are no right or wrong answers ...
minta dia berpikir sambil bicara (think aloud)

fallback.feedback: Contoh: "There are no right or wrong answers. We're testing the app, not you. Just use it as you normally would and think aloud."

n2.them: Okay. So... I'm on the home screen now. What should I try first?
hints: beri tugas: Could you try to ...?

fallback.feedback: Contoh: "Could you try to book a table for two people this Saturday evening?"

n3.them: Hmm, I'm looking for the date... I can't see it anywhere. Is it supposed to be here?
hints: jangan langsung menolong: What would you expect ...?
tanyakan di mana dia akan mencari

fallback.feedback: Contoh: "What would you expect to see here? Where would you look for it?"

n4.them: I'd expect a calendar at the top, like in other apps. Oh, there it is, under 'More options'. That's a bit hidden.
hints: gali perasaannya: How did that make you feel?

fallback.feedback: Contoh: "How did that make you feel? On a scale of one to five, how easy was it?"

n5.them: Honestly, a little frustrated. Maybe a two out of five. Are we done?

fallback.feedback: Contoh: "Almost. Is there anything else you'd change? Thank you, this has been really helpful."

end.them: You're welcome! I hope it helps make the app easier for everyone.
